title: Strict-local complement criterion for regular divisor purity
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $X$ be a regular Noetherian scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $i:D\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular effective Cartier divisor. For every geometric point $\bar x\to D$, let $X_{(\bar x)}$ be the strict henselization of $X$ at its image and let $D_{(\bar x)}=D\times_X X_{(\bar x)}$; write $U_{\bar x}=X_{(\bar x)}\setminus D_{(\bar x)}$. Then the Kummer supported class map $A_D\to i^!A_X(1)[2]$ is an isomorphism if and only if $H^q(U_{\bar x,\mathrm{et}},A)=0$ for every geometric point $\bar x\to D$ and every $q\ge2$. Here an effective Cartier divisor is locally cut out by a single nonzerodivisor; regular means that its scheme $D$ is regular. Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Regularity is [def-weil-regular-scheme], the immersion is [def-weil-closed-immersion], the supported map is [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], the ordinary derived categories and twists are [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist], strict henselizations are [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product], and cohomology is [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: Fix $\bar x\to D$ and put $S=X_{(\bar x)}=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Its ring is strictly henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure]. On an affine open chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\ni x$ with prime $\mathfrak p$, the affine comparison [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] identifies $R$, as a $B$-algebra, with the algebraic strict henselization of $\mathcal O_{X,x}=B_{\mathfrak p}$; hence $R$ is Noetherian and regular by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian, lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular], applied to the regular local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Choose an affine divisor chart at $x$ with equation $f$. Its image $t$ lies in the maximal ideal of $R$ because $x\in D$. The structural ring map is flat by [lem-sbc-affine-strict-henselization-structural-flat]; thus the base-changed closed immersion is regular of codimension one by [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus], so $t$ is a nonzerodivisor. The Cartesian strict-localization identification [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] identifies $D\times_XS$ with the strict localization of $D$ at $\bar x$. Applying the same affine comparison and regularity under strict henselization also to $\mathcal O_{D,x}$ proves that $R/(t)$ is regular. In particular $U_{\bar x}=\operatorname{Spec}R[1/t]$, and $\ell$ remains a unit.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.2, strict-local regular pair; regularity from Stacks Tag 06LN and closed quotient from Tag 05WS

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-strict-local-divisor-low-kummer] to $(R,t,\ell)$. It gives $H^0(U_{\bar x},A)=A$, $H^0(U_{\bar x},A(1))=\mu_\ell(R)$, and $H^1(U_{\bar x},A(1))=A\kappa(t)$ freely on the Kummer class. Choose the primitive root supplied there. The induced isomorphism $A_S\simeq A_S(1)$ restricts to $U_{\bar x}$, so it identifies their cohomology in every degree. Consequently vanishing of $H^q(U_{\bar x},A)$ is equivalent to vanishing of $H^q(U_{\bar x},A(1))$ for each $q$. This choice is used only to test vanishing, not to change the supported class.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.2, low-degree calculation; Stacks Tags 03PL, 0AFZ, 0AG0

proof.text:
Let $j:X-D\hookrightarrow X$. On a divisor chart $j$ is the principal open immersion $D(f)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$, hence $j$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] to $A_X(1)$, take cohomology by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], and take exact geometric stalks by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact]. The closed-stalk identification [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] identifies the first term with cohomology of $(i^!A_X(1))_{\bar x}$. The strict-local direct-image formula [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] identifies the third term in degree $q$ with $H^q(U_{\bar x},A(1))$. The middle term has only degree zero, equal to $A(1)_{\bar x}=\mu_\ell(R)$, and its degree-zero restriction to the third term is the isomorphism of Step 2. The exact sequence therefore gives zero first-term cohomology in degrees $m\leq1$ and isomorphisms
$$\mathcal H^m(i^!A_X(1))_{\bar x}\simeq H^{m-1}(U_{\bar x},A(1))\quad(m\geq2),$$
induced by the localization connecting map. Equivalently, for $B=i^!A_X(1)[2]$, its stalk cohomology vanishes for $r<0$, is $A\kappa(t)$ for $r=0$, and is $H^{r+1}(U_{\bar x},A(1))$ for $r>0$.

The map $\eta:A_D\to B$ in the statement induces an isomorphism in degree zero at $\bar x$. Indeed [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] makes it the transpose of the supported Cartier Kummer map of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], compatibly with strict-local restriction. The definition [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary] realizes that supported class by the Kummer extension of the line bundle with its canonical off-divisor frame. On our principal chart $\mathcal O(D)=t^{-1}R$ has frame $t^{-1}$, and its canonical section $1$ has coordinate $t$. Thus the torsor of $\ell$-th roots of this section is $z^\ell=t$; using the dual frame instead gives $z^\ell=t^{-1}$. To identify the supported splice with the boundary, apply [lem-per-supported-yoneda-localization] to $0\to\mu_\ell\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{(-)^\ell}\mathbf G_m\to0$ and $h=t$ (or $t^{-1}$). Its pushout extension is the frame extension: both are generated by a supported lift of $1$ and by $\mathbf G_m$, with the off-divisor lift fixed by that frame. The supported-Hom identification of [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] then identifies the splice with the connecting image of $\kappa(t)$, up to the frame sign. Therefore $\mathcal H^0(\eta)_{\bar x}$ sends $1$ to $\kappa(t)$ or $-\kappa(t)$ under that identification. Both generate the free rank-one $A$-module of Step 2, including when $\ell=2$. This establishes invertibility of the actual class map, rather than just the rank of its target.

source.place: XVI section 2.1, supported Kummer class, and Proposition 3.4.2, low-degree normalization; the local-frame description is the defining Kummer extension

proof.text: For each $\bar x\to D$, the source $A_D$ has only degree-zero stalk cohomology. Steps 3 and 4 show that $\eta$ induces isomorphisms on all its stalk cohomology groups if and only if $H^{r+1}(U_{\bar x},A(1))=0$ for every $r>0$. Step 2 turns this into precisely $H^q(U_{\bar x},A)=0$ for every $q\geq2$. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] on $D$: $\eta$ is an isomorphism if and only if these conditions hold at every geometric point. If $D$ is empty, the map is the unique morphism between zero objects on the empty site and the quantified condition is vacuous, so the same equivalence holds.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.4.2, conclude by geometric stalks
